title: CONTEXTOR: Contextualized High-order Contrastive Learning
claim: Prior methods give each entity one static embedding that conflates roles across contexts; ours produces context-conditioned, asymmetric representations.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side split by dashed line, top-to-bottom projection into embedding space
description: Two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. Both start with the same entities at the top: Drug1, Gene, Disease1 and Disease2, shown as circular icons on a grey curved band. Panel (a), Existing method: dashed vertical lines project each entity onto a 3D embedding-space plane. This gives one diamond per entity, including a single blue h_Gene. Grey arrows labeled 'pull together' link the gene to Drug1 and Disease1, and to Disease2. Red X marks show that these pulls conflict. Panel (b), CONTEXTOR: the entities feed into a rounded 'CONTEXTOR' box. Dashed purple and red arrows lead from it to two contextualized gene embeddings, h_Gene|Drug1,Disease2 and h_Gene|Drug1,Disease1. Each is matched to a two-color query tuple diamond, and green check marks show the match. Color coding links the contexts to the diamonds.
caption: Comparison between (a) existing methods and (b) CONTEXTOR. Existing methods learn a single static embedding for each entity, which can conflate distinct semantic roles when the same entity (e.g., the gene in the figure) appears in different relational contexts (e.g., disease1 and disease2). In contrast, CONTEXTOR produces context-aware entity representations, enabling flexible and asymmetric high-order relation inference.
abstract: High-order relations involving multiple interacting entities are commonly encountered, particularly in biomedical domains. Existing relational learning methods typically learn static entity representations and assume symmetric relation inference, which can be inadequate for capturing context-dependent entity functions and the inherent asymmetry of high-order relations. In this paper, we propose Contextualized High-order Contrastive Learning (CONTEXTOR), a general and plug-and-play framework that formulates high-order relation inference as a dynamic query–response process. Specifically, CONTEXTOR decomposes each high-order relation into multiple incomplete query tuples and their corresponding response entities. Given a query tuple, we contextualize candidate response entity representations via an asymmetric conditional modulation, and align queries with their corresponding contextualized responses through multi-fold contrastive learning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets spanning multiple biomedical tasks demonstrate that CONTEXTOR consistently outperforms existing methods across diverse evaluation settings. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJUDataIntelligence/CONTEXTOR.
